summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, morbid obesity, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted with fever and an infected right internal jugular hemodialysis catheter. She met criteria for severe sepsis and was found to have MRSA bacteremia. The infected catheter was removed, and a temporary femoral line was placed, later converted to a tunneled left femoral catheter after failed attempts to recanalize the right jugular vein. She was treated with vancomycin, and blood cultures cleared. Concerns for endocarditis and osteomyelitis were ruled out with TEE and clinical monitoring. Constipation and back pain resolved during admission. Warfarin was held during procedures and restarted with heparin bridging until INR was therapeutic. She was discharged to extended care for ongoing dialysis and outpatient antibiotic therapy with close monitoring.
